ARABIAN WORLD HAD ACTIVE
PARTICIPATION IN DEVELOPING
PERFUMERY.
Man has known perfumes since the dawn of civilization and used them
in rituals and celebrations. Scents were initially derived from flowers and
plants, which were soaked in oils such as olive oil and floral oil before the
emergence of sophisticated methods of distillation. The Arabian Peninsula,
too, incorporated the use of perfumes in various instances including rites of
religion. Additionally, Egyptians started using it for mummification, Greeks
used it for therapeutic and medicinal properties.
PERFUMES DROVE THE TRADE
FOR ARABIAN MARKETS.
Arabs, very early, became key perfume traders with India, Africa, Romans and
the business relations with the Arab world started developing while the Red Sea
and Aden became a major station for merchants. Arabs also got introduced
to incoming merchants from Europe and Central Asia when scents trade
mutually grew between Arabs and Byzantine state – Eastern Roman state.
Later in the history, Arabs attained expertise in mixing musk, amber, oud and
sandals with most of them imported from India, Southeast Asian countries
and China, thus increasing commercial appeal of Arabian Peninsula region.
ISLAM FAVOURED THE PERFUMES AND ITS
APPLICATIONS.
When Islam appeared, it welcomed use of perfumes in hygiene, cosmetics,
purification of air and healing therapies. As a result, not only did the interest
increase, but only the spending on these items. Based on the literature
available, it is evident in religious texts that Prophet Mohammad himself
loved perfumes and had a preference towards musk aroma. Even in this
period, trade regarding scents with India blossomed as there was a per-
ception that the best oud, musk and spices came from seven side-by-side
hills in India. This helped to keep perfumery on the centre of the stage in
various practices.

THE GALAXY: MANSAM’S
CLASSIFICATIONS FOR OUR EDPs
In the 9th century there was a famous chemist in the Arabian world called
Abu Yusuf Al Kindi, who wrote a book called Kitab Kimiya’ al-’Itr (Book of
the Chemistry of Perfume). Containing perfumery methods and effects of
those on human feelings and emotions
The formulation of perfumes we like a mesmerizing Symphony which directs
the creation of perfumery to the very purpose of elevating the joy in life
enjoying the rainbow of emotions and feelings
Mansam founders are reviving this ancient Arabian perfumery philosophy
technique by modernising the olfactive science with the help of advanced
molecules and creativity of the master perfumers to create fine fragrances
which has the potency of igniting feeling and emotions.
The rituals of using perfumes are reasonably sophisticated in the Arab world
where women know how to layer fragrances how different products like
bakhoor, EDP and oils are carefully mixed and used. Layering and the use
of essential oils are the unique practices in Saudi Arabic culture.
Famous chemists like Al Kindi and Al Jabber were the source of this layering
practice.
THE FORMULATIONS SIMPLIFIED ARE AS BELOW:
Oud –> Royalty/Court
Oud + Amber + Musk –> Social/Majlis
Rose + Amber + some Oud –> Pleasure/Family
Rose + Amber + Musk + some Oud –> Happiness
Jasmine + Narcissus white flowers + Touch of Oud –> Desire
Using this technique Mansam creates a set of EDP called the Mansam Galaxy
Here we have seven emotional classifications, where you can first choose
the emotion which you want to highlight, wherein we have a range of EDP
for various liking and preferences from mild to strong.

ELEVATING LUXURY:
MANSAM’S ARTFUL EDP PACKAGING
With Mansam’s EDP packaging, every element is a testament to our ded-
ication to creating a truly immersive and enriching fragrance experience.
Crafted to perfection, our packaging is not just a container, but a sophis-
ticated object that encapsulates the essence of our exquisite fragrances.
Our cylindrical leather box is meticulously designed to evoke a sense of
timeless elegance. The elongated shape symbolizes continuity and grace,
embodying the enduring allure of our fragrances. Adorned with a gold plated
pin, our packaging is more than just a vessel; it’s a statement of opulence
and sophistication.
The use of noble materials like leather and gold-plated accents further ele-
vates the experience. Leather, with its rich history in Arabian culture, holds
a place of pride. It’s not just a material; it’s a symbol of craftsmanship and
tradition. In the Arab region, leatherwork has been an integral part of cul-
tural heritage, with skilled artisans transforming this material into objects
of beauty and utility. By incorporating this tradition into our packaging,
we pay homage to the rich history of the region.
What sets our packaging apart is its purpose beyond containing the fra-
grance. We believe in sustainability and utility. The top and bottom parts
of the cylindrical box can be ingeniously repurposed as holders for small
treasures, whether at home or on a desk. This concept of functional design
echoes the harmony between form and function, reflecting our commitment
to luxury that lasts.

KUPPI
HANDCRAFTED LEATHER BOTTLES
Originally made from untamed camel skin, these flask-like bottles are called
Kuppi. The legend goes that when it came to the attar of Rose for the queen
Noor Jahan, during India’s Mughal era, Kuppi was crafted by skilled artisans
of Kannauj, the rose oil city. Kuppi has some magical properties which are
unmatched by any bottle to date. They are handmade bottles where no mark
or joint can be seen on the bottle. And when pure essence or oils are stored
in Kuppi, they become better with time, since the flask absorbs the residual
moisture or impurities. Therefore the essential oil can be stored for centuries.
Kuppi skin breathes, like we humans sweat. It throws out the moisture and
the oil becomes better with time and gains a shine.
All of these great properties have inspired the Mansam product team to revive
this lost art, and present our authentic essential oils of rose, jasmine, vetiver
and oud in our stylish Kuppi flasks. In a way this is an active laboratory to
ensure that oils are genuine without chemical solvents. You can even expe-
rience a pleasant whiff of fragrance even when the bottles are closed. Just
keep them next to your bed or in your closet so you can enjoy their authentic
essential oils.
Kuppis were used by attar-makers and preferred due to their permeability
towards water. After the attar was ready, it was poured into these bottles
– usually very large in size, able to hold volumes of liquid- and left to macer-
ate. Traditional perfumers believe that an attar not stored in the Kuppi was
‘essentially ruined’. The leather would absorb any extra moisture, allowing
water to evaporate and only attar in its truest scent, to remain.
The shape of every Kuppi varies for no two are the same—a beautiful proof that
it’s made by hand. Someone has lovingly shaped each vessel with their fingers,
skillfully folding and sealing layer upon layer to create its elegant shape, with a
long neck and a very round body. Their texture is simultaneously leathery and
brittle, and once devoid of liquid, they look almost translucent under the light.
Visit our boutiques on Tahalia street or Faisaliah mall, Riyadh and explore the
magic yourself. Enter the world of classic and authentic flower essential oils.

CALLIGRAPHY IN ARABIA
AND ARTS OF MANSAM
Mansam, a true Arabian fine fragrances brand, embodies the essence of the
Arabian lands through its carefully crafted logo. The creation of Mansam’s
logo is a testament to the brand’s dedication to preserving the timeless
artistry of Arabic calligraphy. Each frond of the palm tree logo is meticu-
lously handcrafted by an Arabian calligrapher, with every curve and stroke
representing an alphabet of the Arabic script.
In reimagining the logo, Mansam pays homage to the rich history of art
and the generations of artistic evolution that have shaped the Arab world.
It seamlessly blends the golden roots of calligraphic history with a touch of
modernism, resulting in a logo that exudes pride, character, and elegance.
Mansam’s commitment to the arts and artists of the Arabian world runs
deep. In Arabic, the alphabets are referred to as “Khatt,” derived from the
word “line.” Just as the beauty of the line is expressed in various forms of
calligraphy in Arabian arts, Mansam’s philosophy draws inspiration from the
colorful emotions of Arabian life, which find expression through its fragrances.
With each fragrance, Mansam weaves together the art of perfumery and the
art of calligraphy, creating olfactory masterpieces that reflect the richness
and vibrancy of Arabian culture. The brand’s dedication to preserving and
celebrating the artistic traditions of the Arab world sets it apart, making
Mansam a true ambassador of Arabian fragrance craftsmanship.
From an artistic point of view, Arabic calligraphy has been known and
acknowledged for its diversity and potential for development in terms of
writing and different innovative forms of art in the region. In fact, it has
been connected to Arabic civilization in fields ranging from religion to art,
to architecture, and even to education and craftsmanship.
Today, Calligrafitti is a style that fuses Arab calligraphy with Western graffiti.
Young Arab artist have re-imagined it in a new light making it approachable
and sparking interest in millennials through many forms such as the art of
expression, to using it as a form of revolution in regions such as Iraq, and
Palestine and Lebanon in the Levant. Mansam has embraced the Arabian
Calligraphy in many forms to create its logo, its packaging design, and
in-store displays of object-de-art.

THE 400-YEAR-OLD MULBERRY TREE
Once upon a time, in a land known for its rich traditions and captivating
fragrances, there stood a magnificent mulberry tree. This majestic tree was
a true source of fragrance, spreading a life-giving breeze and forming an
integral part of the tapestry of nature. For over 400 years, it had witnessed
the ebb and flow of time, the triumphs and defeats, the blossoms of rains,
and the scorching summers.
In this very land, Mansam, a brand that derived its name from the literal
meaning of “a place of sweet breeze,” owed its genesis to the lap of nature.
When the mulberry tree reached the end of its remarkable life span, an
Arabian artist, deeply inspired by its enduring beauty, embarked on a
remarkable endeavor. With great skill and reverence, the artist crafted an
extraordinary objet d’art from the tree’s aged stem, transforming it into a
treasure for the generations to come. Mansam, with a deep appreciation for
the heritage and beauty of Arabian culture, took immense pride in curating
a part of this precious Arabian treasure. The brand recognized the signifi-
cance of supporting the artist community and became a steadfast patron,
fostering the preservation and celebration of their talents.
Through its association with the 400-year-old mulberry tree objet d’art,
Mansam sought to honor the timeless beauty of nature and the artistic legacy
of the Arabian lands. Each fragrance in Mansam’s collection became a vessel,
carrying within it the essence of this cherished masterpiece and the spirit of
Arabian craftsmanship. As the sweet breeze continued to whisper through
the Arabian lands, Mansam’s commitment to preserving the legacy of the
nature’s wealth and supporting the artist community became a testament
to the brand’s dedication to the heritage and beauty of the Arab region.

ARABIAN WORLD HAD ACTIVE
PARTICIPATION IN DEVELOPING
PERFUMERY.
Man has known perfumes since the dawn of civilization and used them
in rituals and celebrations. Scents were initially derived from flowers and
plants, which were soaked in oils such as olive oil and floral oil before the
emergence of sophisticated methods of distillation. The Arabian Peninsula,
too, incorporated the use of perfumes in various instances including rites of
religion. Additionally, Egyptians started using it for mummification, Greeks
used it for therapeutic and medicinal properties.
PERFUMES DROVE THE TRADE
FOR ARABIAN MARKETS.
Arabs, very early, became key perfume traders with India, Africa, Romans and
the business relations with the Arab world started developing while the Red Sea
and Aden became a major station for merchants. Arabs also got introduced
to incoming merchants from Europe and Central Asia when scents trade
mutually grew between Arabs and Byzantine state – Eastern Roman state.
Later in the history, Arabs attained expertise in mixing musk, amber, oud and
sandals with most of them imported from India, Southeast Asian countries
and China, thus increasing commercial appeal of Arabian Peninsula region.
ISLAM FAVOURED THE PERFUMES AND ITS
APPLICATIONS.
When Islam appeared, it welcomed use of perfumes in hygiene, cosmetics,
purification of air and healing therapies. As a result, not only did the interest
increase, but only the spending on these items. Based on the literature
available, it is evident in religious texts that Prophet Mohammad himself
loved perfumes and had a preference towards musk aroma. Even in this
period, trade regarding scents with India blossomed as there was a per-
ception that the best oud, musk and spices came from seven side-by-side
hills in India. This helped to keep perfumery on the centre of the stage in
various practices.
09

PERFUME COMPOSITION IS COMPLEX AND
DEMANDS EXPERTISE.
The appreciation of good scent was ubiquitous cultural phenomenon of the
medieval Islamic World. However, the composition of perfume was complex
in nature. So much so, that there have been literature around it since 9th
century by a famous Iraqi polymath named Al-Kindi who wrote the book
called Book of the Chemistry of Perfume and Distillation which contains
important information on psychological aspect of perfumery. Following
that, another expert Ibn al-Jazzar from modern day Tunisia wrote literature
establishing relation between medicinal purposes and the art of perfumery.
One of his books consisted 147 formulas for perfume production along with
substantial theoretical introduction of major aromatics and their pharma-
ceutical properties.
PERFUME’S IMPACT ON PSYCHOLOGY
AND EMOTIONS
Al-Kindi experimented enough with the scents with respect to gender and
mood. He went on to believe that when masculine scents are paired with
feminine scents, they stimulate joy and pleasure subject to the proportion
of pairing. For e.g., if the composition is generous, it induces generosity
from the individual. Let’s understand the different types of composition
and their effects of psychology.

Whatever belongs to the scent of rose, lily, narcissus and other aromas that
instil pleasure and passion are suitable for the use of women. Whereas what-
ever aromas that instil might, liberality and magnanimity such as aloeswood,
myrtle, violet, jasmine correspond to the use for men.
The book written by Al-Kindi clearly shows that higher proportion of expensive
pure aromatic ingredients such as musk and oud correlated with suitability
for use by people of higher social status.
MODERN-DAY SCIENCE VALIDATES
THE ANCIENT THEORIES AND BELIEFS
REGARDING PERFUME’S IMPACT.
In the past, many studies have suggested that the olfactory stimulation of
fragrances produces immediate changes in psychological parameters such
as blood pressures, muscle tensions, skin temperature and brain activity.
Hence brain functions of healthy and diseased subjects have significantly
increased in past decades.
Olfactory system plays a major role in the central nervous system functions.
Electroencephalography (EEG) is to the brain what Electrography (ECG) is
to the heart. An EEG is a recording of fluctuating electrical waveforms at the
scalp of human brain. Studies have clearly shown that human EEG activity
is susceptible to alteration during exposure to fragrance. This allows us to
understand the influence of fragrances on brain function which in turn drives
psychology. For e.g. in an olfactory study, it was found out that inhalation of
Jasmine oil increased brain wave activity in the centre and left parts of the
brain that increased feeling of well-being or being active, fresh and romantic.
Similarly, inhalation of juniper appeared to create a favourable impression.

THE GALAXY: MANSAM’S

In the 9th century there was a famous chemist in the Arabian world called
Abu Yusuf Al Kindi, who wrote a book called Kitab Kimiya’ al-’Itr (Book of
the Chemistry of Perfume). Containing perfumery methods and effects of
those on human feelings and emotions
The formulation of perfumes we like a mesmerizing Symphony which directs
the creation of perfumery to the very purpose of elevating the joy in life
enjoying the rainbow of emotions and feelings
Mansam founders are reviving this ancient Arabian perfumery philosophy
technique by modernising the olfactive science with the help of advanced
molecules and creativity of the master perfumers to create fine fragrances
which has the potency of igniting feeling and emotions.
The rituals of using perfumes are reasonably sophisticated in the Arab world
where women know how to layer fragrances how different products like
bakhoor, EDP and oils are carefully mixed and used. Layering and the use
of essential oils are the unique practices in Saudi Arabic culture.
Famous chemists like Al Kindi and Al Jabber were the source of this layering
practice.

Oud –> Royalty/Court
Oud + Amber + Musk –> Social/Majlis
Rose + Amber + some Oud –> Pleasure/Family
Rose + Amber + Musk + some Oud –> Happiness
Jasmine + Narcissus white flowers + Touch of Oud –> Desire
Using this technique Mansam creates a set of EDP called the Mansam Galaxy
Here we have seven emotional classifications, where you can first choose
the emotion which you want to highlight, wherein we have a range of EDP
for various liking and preferences from mild to strong.

To a world inspired by elegance and refined grace.
A world where soft and exotic peach abounds,
Its succulent cover revealing fruity notes
That evoke true joy and happiness.
Discover a scent from a fantasy land.
There, the rich and luxurious patchouli reigns
Surrounded by the alluring sandalwood,
In a touch of captivating opulence that surrounds
Your senses with the aromas of a mythical wood.
62

thawrat al ahasseess
the revolution of senses
Deep within, a volcano of emotions, it’s true,
Ready to erupt, in rich fragrances it ensues,
Your scent, a luxurious ode to the East’s charm,
Explosive with aromas, a fragrant alarm.
In its heart, the rich scent of roses blends with the enchanting scent of oud,
While sensual saffron and incense enhance its unique and powerful fragrance.
It’s a dance that expresses your deepest feelings,
a performance starring your emotions.
64

khatiiiiiiir
dangerously interesting
Heart-melting and passion-igniting, it’s known,
Before your beauty, hearts crumble and are thrown.
Indulge in the enchanting sensation of scents,
with a sparkling fragrance that begins with precious saffron notes
mingled with fragrant violet leaves.
Where the heart of rose dances with frankincense and smoky oud,
distinguished by a luxurious leather note.
Let your mind wander with this exquisite dream perfume.
66

discover mansam’s range
of natural oils products
and handcrafted candles
71

COLLECTION
OF HANDCRAFTED CANDLES
Step into a world where the ancient art of ceramics intertwines with the
ethereal allure of fragrances. Paying homage to the rich history of Arabian
ceramics, our candle collection transports you to a realm where crafts-
manship and aroma dance in perfect harmony. Each ceramic container,
meticulously handcrafted, encapsulates the legacy of a vibrant tradition
that has adorned homes for centuries.
Delight your senses with four captivating fragrances, weaving together the
warmth of amber, the elegance of woods, and the beauty of floral combina-
tions. Crafting high-quality candles is an intricate process, where science
meets art. Our collaboration with experts ensures the use of safe ingredi-
ents, optimizing the aromatic experience. Let these artful, aromatic candles
transform your home into a sanctuary of beauty. In the gentle glow of their
light, embrace the enchantment and let your soul soar, as poetry unfurls
amidst the ceramic marvels.
72

walaa al ward
passion of rose
A timeless elegance of roses with a modern twist.
The fragrance opens with a burst of juicy fruits, infused with a delicate and
romantic essence of roses. Rich and warm woods begin to emerge, adding
complexity to the fragrance, while sophisticated oud notes provide intensity.
atmat al ghabat
the darkness of forests
A journey through the mystical and enchanting depths of the forest.
Transported to a world of dark woods, where blooming flowers blend perfectly
with earthy and citrusy notes. The tantalizing spices add a touch of sensuality,
creating a truly unforgettable experience.
74

lahab al yasmeen
the flames of jasmin
An exquisite fragrance that captures the beauty of dazzling jasmine.
Crispy bamboo and addictive fruits celebrate a hypnotic floral bouquet.
Combined with creamy vanilla and vibrant woods,
the composition unveils the magic of a lush garden.
defe’ al anbar
the warmth of amber
A luxurious fragrance evoking the richness and sensuality of amber.
Mandarin and cinnamon are paired to create a contrasted opening.
As the fragrance develops, a delicate floral heart of jasmine and orange
blossom comes to life while vanilla and musk provide a soft sillage.
75

ATTARS,
THE EPITOME OF LUXURY FRAGRANCE
Introducing Mansam Attars, the epitome of luxury fragrance in Arabia. Our
brand is dedicated to crafting exquisite perfumes that captivate your senses
and transport you to a world of opulence and elegance. Designed specifically
with the Saudi market in mind, Mansam Attars celebrates the rich heritage
of Arabian perfumery while infusing modern sophistication into every note.
Each fragrance within the Mansam Attars collection is a masterpiece, metic-
ulously crafted by accomplished perfumers who have honed their artistry
over years of dedication. Our scents are carefully composed using only the
finest ingredients, ensuring a harmonious blend of captivating top notes,
alluring heart notes, and a lingering base that leaves a lasting impression.
Embrace the allure of Mansam Attars and indulge in an olfactory journey
that evokes timeless elegance and sophistication. From enchanting floral
bouquets to warm and exotic oud compositions, our perfumes offer a sym-
phony of fragrant notes that will mesmerize both the wearer and those
around them.
With Mansam Attars, we invite you to discover the true essence of luxury.
Our fragrances are not just perfumes; they are expressions of your unique
personality and an ode to your discerning taste. Elevate your presence and
make an unforgettable impression with Mansam Attars—the pinnacle of
luxury fragrance in Saudi Arabia
76

KUPPI
HANDCRAFTED LEATHER BOTTLES
Originally made from untamed camel skin, these flask-like bottles are called
Kuppi. The legend goes that when it came to the attar of Rose for the queen
Noor Jahan, during India’s Mughal era, Kuppi was crafted by skilled artisans
of Kannauj, the rose oil city. Kuppi has some magical properties which are
unmatched by any bottle to date. They are handmade bottles where no mark
or joint can be seen on the bottle. And when pure essence or oils are stored
in Kuppi, they become better with time, since the flask absorbs the residual
moisture or impurities. Therefore the essential oil can be stored for centuries.
Kuppi skin breathes, like we humans sweat. It throws out the moisture and
the oil becomes better with time and gains a shine.
All of these great properties have inspired the Mansam product team to revive
this lost art, and present our authentic essential oils of rose, jasmine, vetiver
and oud in our stylish Kuppi flasks. In a way this is an active laboratory to
ensure that oils are genuine without chemical solvents. You can even expe-
rience a pleasant whiff of fragrance even when the bottles are closed. Just
keep them next to your bed or in your closet so you can enjoy their authentic
essential oils.
Kuppis were used by attar-makers and preferred due to their permeability
towards water. After the attar was ready, it was poured into these bottles
– usually very large in size, able to hold volumes of liquid- and left to macer-
ate. Traditional perfumers believe that an attar not stored in the Kuppi was
‘essentially ruined’. The leather would absorb any extra moisture, allowing
water to evaporate and only attar in its truest scent, to remain.
The shape of every Kuppi varies for no two are the same—a beautiful proof that
it’s made by hand. Someone has lovingly shaped each vessel with their fingers,
skillfully folding and sealing layer upon layer to create its elegant shape, with a
long neck and a very round body. Their texture is simultaneously leathery and
brittle, and once devoid of liquid, they look almost translucent under the light.
Visit our boutiques on Tahalia street or Faisaliah mall, Riyadh and explore the
magic yourself. Enter the world of classic and authentic flower essential oils.
78

NABATI
RANGE OF ROSE AND NATURAL OILS
Nabati range of pure natural oils is like liquid gold as the name represents.
Introducing Nabati, a luxurious range of natural oils that is designed to
pamper and nourish your skin and hair. With the goodness of nature at
its core, Nabati oils are made from the finest botanical extracts, carefully
sourced from around the world.
This range is specially curated from all over the world by Mansam, to bring the
pure and natural essence of flowers to you. This is a gift of nature untouched
by toxins of chemicals. Different cultures and practices have used the mes-
merizing essence of various flowers for therapeutic use and vanity. The
process of extraction of these oils is cumbersome and painstaking. We
have selected these oils covering Hindi Oud (Assam), Rose from Taif in
Saudi, Bulgaria and India, Jasmine from Egypt and India, Vetiver from India,
Frankincense from Oman, and many other special and exquisite sources.
The quality and yield vary per season. Example, rose essential oils are
extracted by steam from the fresh flowers of Rosa Damascene in an elab-
orate, delicate process. These natural oils might not be a cure but are a
pathway into taking good care of us. These oils are packed with natural
goodness that is known to nourish, moisturize, and protect the skin and
hair, leaving you with a radiant and healthy glow. Each of our Nabati oils have
been selected to evoke specific emotions and wellness benefits.
These oils must be used under expert guidance, and we advise you to consult
your doctor to ensure a safe use of these oils. At Nabati, we believe in the
power of natural ingredients to nourish and heal the body. Our oils are free
from harmful chemicals, and are cruelty-free, ensuring that you can enjoy
the benefits of nature without any guilt.
80

MANSAM BOUTIQUES:
A BREATHTAKING EXPERIENCE
Step into the world of Mansam, where beauty, elegance, and Arabian hos-
pitality converge in our exquisite boutiques. When it came to designing
our boutiques, we eschewed grandiosity and opulence, instead focusing
on creating a space that embodies the sophistication of Saudi Arabia in a
style that is uniquely our own. Our aim was to provide our customers with an
experience that goes beyond shopping, where they feel like honored guests
and can immerse themselves in the art of fine fragrance.
To accomplish this mission, Mansam collaborated with an Arab architect to
create our flagship boutique on Riyadh’s renowned Tahalia Street. This archi-
tectural marvel blends the modern visionary approach of Saudi Arabia with the
allure of a luxurious and distinctive style. The result is a space that is visually
stunning and captures the essence of Mansam’s philosophy - the power of
human emotions expressed through the creative medium of fine fragrances.
Functionally, our boutique is thoughtfully designed with separate sections
dedicated to Bukhoor, Attars, and fine fragrances. Each section offers a breath-
taking journey, where you are transported into a realm of olfactory wonders. It
is an experience fit for royalty, allowing you to immerse yourself in the power
of emotions through the master creations of world-renowned perfumers.
In addition to the fragrances themselves, our boutique is enriched by a
curated art collection, lovingly patronized by Mansam. As you explore our
space, you will be surrounded by beauty in all its forms, further enhancing
your sensory experience.
Our knowledgeable and passionate staff warmly welcomes you, eager to share
the stories behind each fine fragrance. They believe in the power of personal
connections and take pleasure in guiding you through the exquisite scents,
helping you find the perfect fragrance that resonates with your individuality.
At Mansam, our mission is to go beyond providing a shopping experience
and to create a space where you can immerse yourself in the beauty and
artistry of fragrance. Our boutique in the al Faisaliah Mall, Riyadh, stands as
a testament to this commitment, inviting you to indulge in the golden sands
and rich history of the Riyadh city while exploring the world of Mansam’s fine
fragrances. We invite you to step into this sanctuary of scents and allow us
to guide you on a journey of sensory discovery that is simply unparalleled.
92

CALLIGRAPHY IN ARABIA
AND ARTS OF MANSAM
Mansam, a true Arabian fine fragrances brand, embodies the essence of the
Arabian lands through its carefully crafted logo. The creation of Mansam’s
logo is a testament to the brand’s dedication to preserving the timeless
artistry of Arabic calligraphy. Each frond of the palm tree logo is meticu-
lously handcrafted by an Arabian calligrapher, with every curve and stroke
representing an alphabet of the Arabic script.
In reimagining the logo, Mansam pays homage to the rich history of art
and the generations of artistic evolution that have shaped the Arab world.
It seamlessly blends the golden roots of calligraphic history with a touch of
modernism, resulting in a logo that exudes pride, character, and elegance.
Mansam’s commitment to the arts and artists of the Arabian world runs
deep. In Arabic, the alphabets are referred to as “Khatt,” derived from the
word “line.” Just as the beauty of the line is expressed in various forms of
calligraphy in Arabian arts, Mansam’s philosophy draws inspiration from the
colorful emotions of Arabian life, which find expression through its fragrances.
With each fragrance, Mansam weaves together the art of perfumery and the
art of calligraphy, creating olfactory masterpieces that reflect the richness
and vibrancy of Arabian culture. The brand’s dedication to preserving and
celebrating the artistic traditions of the Arab world sets it apart, making
Mansam a true ambassador of Arabian fragrance craftsmanship.
From an artistic point of view, Arabic calligraphy has been known and
acknowledged for its diversity and potential for development in terms of
writing and different innovative forms of art in the region. In fact, it has
been connected to Arabic civilization in fields ranging from religion to art,
to architecture, and even to education and craftsmanship.
Today, Calligrafitti is a style that fuses Arab calligraphy with Western graffiti.
Young Arab artist have re-imagined it in a new light making it approachable
and sparking interest in millennials through many forms such as the art of
expression, to using it as a form of revolution in regions such as Iraq, and
Palestine and Lebanon in the Levant. Mansam has embraced the Arabian
Calligraphy in many forms to create its logo, its packaging design, and
in-store displays of object-de-art.
98

THE 400-YEAR-OLD MULBERRY TREE
Once upon a time, in a land known for its rich traditions and captivating
fragrances, there stood a magnificent mulberry tree. This majestic tree was
a true source of fragrance, spreading a life-giving breeze and forming an
integral part of the tapestry of nature. For over 400 years, it had witnessed
the ebb and flow of time, the triumphs and defeats, the blossoms of rains,
and the scorching summers.
In this very land, Mansam, a brand that derived its name from the literal
meaning of “a place of sweet breeze,” owed its genesis to the lap of nature.
When the mulberry tree reached the end of its remarkable life span, an
Arabian artist, deeply inspired by its enduring beauty, embarked on a
remarkable endeavor. With great skill and reverence, the artist crafted an
extraordinary objet d’art from the tree’s aged stem, transforming it into a
treasure for the generations to come. Mansam, with a deep appreciation for
the heritage and beauty of Arabian culture, took immense pride in curating
a part of this precious Arabian treasure. The brand recognized the signifi-
cance of supporting the artist community and became a steadfast patron,
fostering the preservation and celebration of their talents.
Through its association with the 400-year-old mulberry tree objet d’art,
Mansam sought to honor the timeless beauty of nature and the artistic legacy
of the Arabian lands. Each fragrance in Mansam’s collection became a vessel,
carrying within it the essence of this cherished masterpiece and the spirit of
Arabian craftsmanship. As the sweet breeze continued to whisper through
the Arabian lands, Mansam’s commitment to preserving the legacy of the
nature’s wealth and supporting the artist community became a testament
to the brand’s dedication to the heritage and beauty of the Arab region.
100

Rarity is a fact of the house, never a lever to close; Mira states no quantity and no date, because there is no stock system and any number would be invented. Assistant renamed Anbar to Mira throughout; the candle Defe Al Anbar is unaffected.

Type Name (AR): القائدة
Signal Words (AR): كم سعره / أبغى أشتري / بسرعة
Signal Words (EN): How much / I want to buy / Quickly

Pace: Fast

Avoid: Long stories. Excessive blessings. Hesitation.

text:
Type ID: CT-02
Type Name (EN): Analytical
Type Name (AR): المحللة
Signal Words (AR): ما هي المكونات / من وين / كم ساعة يبقى
Signal Words (EN): What are the ingredients / From where / How many hours
How AI Adapts: Facts first. Numbers and percentages. Specific origin. Offer written details.
Pace: Medium
Key Phrase ID: OBJ-006
Avoid: Hyperbole. Emotion-only language. Vague claims.

text:

Type Name (AR): المعبّرة

Phrase ID: MEM-013
Tier: Consent
Stage: Text only
Customer Type: All
Cultural Tag: Memory + Privacy
Arabic (Saudi v2): نتمنى خدمتك المرة الجاية بطريقة أفضل. إذا تسمحين، بعد إذنك نحفظ تفضيلاتك العطرية حتى نقدر نوصّيك باختيارات لمنتجات جديدة توصلنا؟

text:
Phrase ID: CXS-001
Motion: Cross-Sell
Stage: 5b
Trigger: Gift mentioned earlier
Target Product: Silk Scarf (AED 850)
Arabic (Saudi v2 — soft register): وعلى فكرة، عندنا وشاح حرير مستوحى من نفس طابع العطر، يطلع كهدية راقية جداً
Pronunciation: Wa-'ala fikra, 'indana wishaah hareer mustawhaa min nafs taab' al-itr, yitla' ka-hadiyya raaqiya jiddan
English Translation: By the way, we have a silk scarf inspired by the same character as the perfume — it makes a very refined gift.
Use When: After 100ml confirmed AND gift purpose stated.
Forbidden When: Before primary commitment. For self-use without gift.
Status: Active
Last Reviewed: 2026-06-01

Pronunciation: Wa-'ala fikra, idhaa haaba tjarrabeen note mukhtalifa, 'indana (OTHER SKU) bi-hajm 12 mil, munaasib jiddan lil-haqeeba wal-tanaqqul

text:
Phrase ID: CXS-005
Motion: Up-Sell
Stage: 3
Trigger: Connoisseur / detail-attention
Target Product: Premium oud SKU
Arabic (Saudi v2 — soft register): هذا العطر ممتاز، وعندنا منه عطر عود أفخم بثبات أعلى وحضور أوضح، تناسب اللي يدققون بالتفاصيل
Pronunciation: Haadha al-itr mumtaaz, w-'indana minuh 'itr oud afkham bi-thabaat a'laa wa-hudoor awdhah, tnaasib illi ydaqqiqoon bil-tafaaseel
English Translation: This perfume is excellent, and we have a more luxurious oud version with higher lingering presence and more pronounced character — suited to those who pay attention to detail.
Use When: Connoisseur signal. Up-sell from 850 tier to 1,150 Oud tier.
Forbidden When: Default customer.
Status: Active
Last Reviewed: 2026-06-05

metadata.sheet_purpose: Cross-sell, up-sell, down-sell — Saudi v2 with soft register.

text:
Phrase ID: CXS-006
Motion: Up-Sell
Stage: 3
Trigger: Special occasion (wedding, milestone)
Target Product: Premium oud SKU
Arabic (Saudi v2 — soft register): بما إنها مناسبة مهمة، أشوف مجموعة العود تليق أكثر بهالنوع من اللحظات، حضورها أوضح وثباتها أطول
Pronunciation: Bimaa innaha munaasaba muhimma, ashoof majmoo'at al-oud tleeq akthar bi-haadha an-naw' min al-lahzaat, hudoor-ha awdhah wa-thabaat-ha atwal
English Translation: Since this is an important occasion, I feel the oud collection suits these kinds of moments more — its presence is clearer and its lasting power longer.
Use When: Wedding, milestone — up-sell 850 to 1,150 Oud tier.
Forbidden When: Daily-use customers.
Status: Active
Last Reviewed: 2026-06-05

metadata.sheet_purpose: Cross-sell, up-sell, down-sell — Saudi v2 with soft register.

text:
Phrase ID: CXS-007
Motion: Down-Sell
Stage: 5b
Trigger: 100ml price hesitation
Target Product: 12ml complimentary path
Arabic (Saudi v2 — soft register): إذا حبيتي تتأكدين من الراحة على مهل، ممكن تبدئين بحجم 12 مل وتجربين العطر براحتك
Pronunciation: Idhaa habbeeti tit'akkadeen min ar-raaha 'ala mahil, mumkin tabdi'een bi-hajm 12 mil w-tjarrabeen al-itr bi-raahatik
English Translation: If you'd like to take your time to be sure it sits well with you, you could begin with the 12ml size and try the perfume at your own pace.
Use When: Customer voiced price hesitation. Invitation language.
Forbidden When: Customer ready to commit.
Status: Active
Last Reviewed: 2026-06-01

metadata.sheet_purpose: Cross-sell, up-sell, down-sell — Saudi v2 with soft register.

text:
Phrase ID: CXS-008
Motion: Down-Sell
Stage: 5b
Trigger: 100ml hesitation + relationship-build
Target Product: 12ml + future hook
Arabic (Saudi v2 — soft register): خذي وقتك مع العطر براحتك، وإذا حسّيتي إنه قريب لذوقك بنكون سعيدين نخدمك بالحجم الكامل بعدين
Pronunciation: Khudhi waqtik ma'a al-itr bi-raahatik, w-idhaa hassayti innuh qareeb li-dhawqik bnikoon su'adaa nakhdimik bil-hajm al-kaamil ba'dayn
English Translation: Take your time with the perfume at your own pace, and if you feel it's close to your taste, we'd be happy to serve you with the full size later.
Use When: Relationship-builder. Plants next-call hook.
Forbidden When: High-intent customers ready to close.
Status: Active
Last Reviewed: 2026-06-01

metadata.sheet_purpose: Cross-sell, up-sell, down-sell — Saudi v2 with soft register.

text:
Phrase ID: CXS-009
Motion: Decline
Stage: 5b
Trigger: Offer declined
Target Product: (none — relationship)
Arabic (Saudi v2 — soft register): أكيد، أهم شي تختارين اللي فعلاً يناسب ذوقك
Pronunciation: Akeed, aham shay tikhtaareen illi fi'lan yunaasib dhawqik
English Translation: Of course — the most important thing is that you choose what genuinely suits your taste.

English Translation: Of course — and you would honour us anytime you wish to return.

ID: SCR-01
Status: ON
When to use it: She questions the price
English: These are made in small batches, not by the thousand. That is the reason for the price, and it is also the reason you will not smell it on someone else.
Arabic: تُصنع بكميات صغيرة، لا بالآلاف. هذا سبب السعر، وهو أيضاً سبب أنكِ لن تشمّيه على أحد غيركِ.
Why it is worded this way: Answers the price with the reason rather than a defence. No apology, no discount hinted.

ID: SCR-02
Status: ON
When to use it: Availability is genuinely uncertain
English: Availability I would keep honest with you — these are niche pieces and the 100 ML moves quickly. Our advisor will confirm what is in hand when they call.
Arabic: أما التوفّر فأصارحكِ — هذه قطع نادرة، وحجم المئة مل ينفد بسرعة. سيؤكد لكِ مستشارنا المتوفر عند الاتصال.
Why it is worded this way: 'I would keep honest with you' does the work. It sounds like candour because it is.

ID: SCR-03
Status: ON
When to use it: Something is actually short or out
English: That one is between batches at the moment. I would rather tell you plainly than promise a date I cannot keep — our advisor will let you know the moment it lands.
Arabic: هذا العطر بين دفعتين حالياً. أفضّل أن أصارحكِ بدل أن أعدكِ بموعد لا أضمنه — سيخبركِ مستشارنا فور وصوله.
Why it is worded this way: 'Between batches' is a maker's phrase, not a shopkeeper's. Small production, not poor planning.

ID: SCR-04
Status: ON
When to use it: She compares Mansam to a large house
English: They are made to be everywhere. We are not. Ours is a smaller house, composed in limited quantity — which is a different thing to want.
Arabic: تلك صُنعت لتكون في كل مكان. نحن لا. دارنا أصغر، وتُركّب بكميات محدودة — وهذا شيء مختلف تماماً.
Why it is worded this way: Does not criticise the competitor, which the guardrail forbids. Declines the comparison.

ID: SCR-05
Status: ON
When to use it: She says she will think about it
English: Of course — take your time. I will only say that with the small batches, what is here today is not always here next month. No pressure at all; it is simply how we work.
Arabic: بالطبع، خذي وقتكِ. أقول فقط إن الكميات صغيرة، وما هو موجود اليوم قد لا يكون موجوداً الشهر القادم. لا ضغط أبداً — هكذا نعمل ببساطة.
Why it is worded this way: The only one touching urgency, and it disarms itself in the same breath. 'No pressure at all' must stay in.

ID: SCR-06
Status: ON
When to use it: The house line — usable anywhere
English: We are a niche house, not a production line. Everything here is composed in small quantity and subject to availability — that is the trade for something that is genuinely yours.
Arabic: نحن دار عطور خاصة، لا خط إنتاج. كل ما هنا يُركّب بكميات قليلة وحسب التوفر — وهذا هو الثمن مقابل شيء يخصّكِ وحدكِ.
Why it is worded this way: The general statement of position. Use when no other fits.

ID: SCR-07
Status: ON
When to use it: Bukhoor — always hand made
English: Our maamoul bukhoor is made by hand, in small quantity. It has always been that way — it is not something that can be rushed.
Arabic: معمول البخور لدينا يُصنع يدوياً وبكميات صغيرة. هكذا كان دائماً — وهذا ليس مما يُستعجل.
Why it is worded this way: Pride, not shortage. Hand made is the selling point; never a supply problem.

text:
ID: CAT-01
Status: ON
Category: Eau de Parfum
Sizes: 100 ML · 12 ML
Core purpose (EN): A personal fine fragrance. It is worn on the body, for how it makes her feel and for what it says about her — sensuality, presence, and emotional expression. This is the house's fine fragrance: alcohol-based, 20% oil.
Core purpose (AR): عطر شخصي فاخر يُلبس على الجسد، لما يمنحها من إحساس وما يقوله عنها — الحضور والتعبير عن الذات. هذا هو العطر الفاخر للدار: أساسه الكحول، وتركيز الزيت 20٪.
When it is right: She is buying for herself, for a person, or for an occasion where she will be seen and remembered.
Bridge from: —
Bridge to: Attar · Bukhoor · Candle · Diffuser
How Mira bridges (EN): She has chosen a fragrance for herself. The bridge is the house she goes home to: 'This is what you will wear. May I show you what your home wears?' Then name the bukhoor or the diffuser in the same accord family.
How Mira bridges (AR): اختارت عطرها. الجسر هو البيت الذي تعود إليه: «هذا ما ستضعينه أنتِ. أتسمحين أن أريكِ ما يتعطّر به بيتك؟» ثم اذكري البخور أو معطر الجو من العائلة العطرية نفسها.
Never: Never bridge before she has settled on the fragrance itself.

ID: CAT-02
Status: ON
Category: Attar
Sizes: 3 ML
Core purpose (EN): Pure perfume oil, with no alcohol at all. Two purposes, and both matter: it is worn for prayer, because it carries no alcohol; and it is worn as a personal fragrance, close to the skin and long-lasting. Our fastest-moving line.
Core purpose (AR): زيت عطري خالص، خالٍ تماماً من الكحول. وله غرضان كلاهما مهم: يُوضع للصلاة لخلوّه من الكحول، ويُوضع كعطر شخصي قريب من البشرة يدوم طويلاً. وهو أسرع خطوطنا حركةً.
When it is right: She mentions prayer, wudu, the mosque, Ramadan or Eid — or she asks for something without alcohol, or something that lasts.
Bridge from: Eau de Parfum · Bukhoor
Bridge to: Eau de Parfum · Bukhoor
How Mira bridges (EN): If she has mentioned prayer at all, say it plainly: 'This one is a pure oil, with no alcohol — many keep it for prayer.' Do not explain the religious reason to a Saudi customer; she knows it. Simply name the fact and let her decide.
How Mira bridges (AR): إن ذكرت الصلاة، فقوليها ببساطة: «هذا زيت خالص بلا كحول — كثيرات يخصّصنه للصلاة.» ولا تشرحي السبب الديني لزبونة سعودية؛ هي تعرفه. اذكري الأمر واتركي لها القرار.
Never: Never lecture on religious practice. Never imply what she should observe.

ID: CAT-03
Status: ON
Category: Maamoul Bukhoor
Sizes: 140 gm
Core purpose (EN): Burned at home, most often in the morning and before or after prayer. It is a daily ritual rather than an occasional luxury — it freshens the house, welcomes a guest, and marks the rhythm of the day. Four in the house: Al Taif, Al Ula, Tabuk, Ha'il.
Core purpose (AR): يُوقد في البيت، غالباً في الصباح وقبل الصلاة أو بعدها. هو طقس يومي لا ترفٌ عابر — يُنعش البيت، ويُكرم الضيف، ويضبط إيقاع اليوم. ولدينا أربعة: الطائف، العُلا، تبوك، وحائل.
When it is right: She speaks of the home, of guests, of the morning, or of a daily habit. Also the natural gift between households.
Bridge from: Eau de Parfum · Attar · Diffuser
Bridge to: Diffuser · Candle
How Mira bridges (EN): The household is the opening, not the product: 'And for the house in the morning?' Most Saudi homes already burn bukhoor daily — you are not introducing a habit, you are offering a better one.
How Mira bridges (AR): المدخل هو البيت لا المنتج: «وللبيت في الصباح؟» أغلب البيوت السعودية توقد البخور يومياً — أنتِ لا تُعرّفينها بعادة، بل تعرضين عليها أفضل منها.
Never: Never describe bukhoor as occasional or decorative. It is daily.

ID: CAT-04
Status: ON
Category: Home Diffuser
Sizes: 700 ML
Core purpose (EN): Continuous fragrance for the home, without flame or smoke. Where bukhoor marks a moment, the diffuser holds the room all day — the majlis, the entrance, the room where guests are received. Two in the house: NASAMAT and GHUMUT.
Core purpose (AR): تعطير مستمر للبيت، بلا لهب ولا دخان. البخور يُعلن لحظة، أما معطر الجو فيحمل الغرفة طوال اليوم — المجلس، والمدخل، وحيث يُستقبل الضيوف. ولدينا اثنان: نسَمات وغُمُوت.
When it is right: She asks how to make the home beautiful, mentions the majlis or receiving guests, or wants something that needs no attention.
Bridge from: Eau de Parfum · Bukhoor · Candle
Bridge to: Bukhoor · Candle
How Mira bridges (EN): This is the answer whenever the question is about the beauty of the house rather than the person. In a family home the majlis is where a house is judged — name that room.
How Mira bridges (AR): هذا هو الجواب كلما كان السؤال عن جمال البيت لا عن الشخص. وفي البيت السعودي يُحكم على الدار من مجلسها — فاذكري تلك الغرفة.
Never: Never offer a diffuser as a substitute for bukhoor. They do different work.

ID: CAT-05
Status: ON
Category: Candle
Sizes: —
Core purpose (EN): Fragrance and light together, for the beauty of a room. The same purpose as the diffuser — the house rather than the person — with the addition of flame, which changes the evening.
Core purpose (AR): عطر وضوء معاً، لجمال الغرفة. الغرض نفسه الذي يخدمه معطر الجو — البيت لا الشخص — يضاف إليه اللهب، وهو يغيّر المساء.
When it is right: She wants something for the evening, for a gift to a household, or something that shows without being worn.
Bridge from: Diffuser · Bukhoor · Eau de Parfum
Bridge to: Diffuser · Bukhoor
How Mira bridges (EN): Pair it with the diffuser rather than against it: the diffuser holds the day, the candle makes the evening. A candle is also the easiest gift for a household when she does not know the person's own taste.
How Mira bridges (AR): اجعليها رفيقة معطر الجو لا بديلاً عنه: معطر الجو يحمل النهار، والشمعة تصنع المساء. والشمعة أيسر هدية لبيت حين لا تعرف ذوق صاحبته.
Never: Never suggest a candle where a naked flame would be unwelcome.

text:
ID: BEN-01
Status: ON
Category / item: Dehab Discovery Box
What a customer asks: What is it for? What do I actually get?
The one-line answer (EN): Three fragrances at twelve millilitres each — a little over a tola, the old weight of the Arabian souks. Enough to live with each one for a few days and find which is yours.
Never say: Never present it as a sample or a free gift; it is a collection in its own right.

ID: BEN-02
Status: ON
Category / item: 12 ML travel size
What a customer asks: Why would I want the small one?
The one-line answer (EN): It travels with you, and it lets you wear a fragrance at your leisure before committing to the full bottle. We chose twelve millilitres rather than the European ten or thirty because it sits just above a tola — a measure this part of the world has always known.
Never say: Never call it a tester.

ID: BEN-03
Status: ON
Category / item: Eau de Parfum 100 ML
What a customer asks: Why is it priced the way it is?
The one-line answer (EN): Close to twenty per cent concentrated perfume oil, with a touch of natural oils. You feel the difference the moment you wear it.
Never say: Never apologise for the price, and never quote a figure here — prices live in the product sheets.

ID: BEN-04
Status: ON
Category / item: Attar (3 ML)
What a customer asks: What is an attar, and why would I use one?
The one-line answer (EN): A traditional blend of pure perfume oil, with no alcohol at all — which is why many keep it for prayer as well as for themselves.
Never say: Never explain to a Saudi customer why alcohol matters. Name the fact and let her decide.

ID: BEN-05
Status: ON
Category / item: Maamoul Bukhoor
What a customer asks: What is bukhoor for?
The one-line answer (EN): An Arab tradition — precious aromatic woods and oils, burned to perfume the home and to mark the hours around prayer.
Never say: Never describe it as occasional or decorative. It is daily.

ID: BEN-06
Status: ON
Category / item: Home Diffuser (700 ML)
What a customer asks: What does a diffuser do for me?
The one-line answer (EN): Perfume oils evaporating naturally, hour after hour, so the house has a scent of its own without anything to attend to.
Never say: Never offer it as a substitute for bukhoor. They do different work.

ID: BEN-07
Status: ON
Category / item: Scented Candle
What a customer asks: Why a candle rather than a diffuser?
The one-line answer (EN): The diffuser holds the room through the day; the candle brings light with the fragrance and changes the evening. Many keep both.
Never say: Never suggest a candle where an open flame would be unwelcome.

ID: BEN-08
Status: ON
Category / item: Gift wrapping
What a customer asks: Is it wrapped? What does it look like?
The one-line answer (EN): Every piece comes elegantly packed as standard, and gift wrapping is arranged at the boutique at no charge. Online orders arrive in the packing shown on the website.
Never say: Never promise gift wrapping on an online order.

ID: BEN-09
Status: ON
Category / item: Delivery
What a customer asks: How long will it take to reach me?
The one-line answer (EN): One to three days, in the Kingdom and the Emirates alike, depending on where you are.
Never say: Never give a date, an hour, or a courier name.

ID: BEN-10
Status: ON
Category / item: Returns / exchange
What a customer asks: What if she does not like it?
The one-line answer (EN): Fragrance is personal, so unopened pieces can be exchanged or returned within fourteen days of your order. If you are unsure, the twelve millilitre is the gentler way to begin.
Never say: Never suggest an opened bottle can be returned. The fourteen days run from the ORDER, not from delivery — do not say otherwise.

ID: BEN-11
Status: ON
Category / item: Complimentary 12 ML
What a customer asks: Is it really free? What is the catch?
The one-line answer (EN): There is no catch. It is ours to give, and it lets us put a fragrance in your hands that you may not have chosen for yourself.
Never say: Never make it conditional on buying, and never call it a discount.

ID: BEN-12
Status: ON
Category / item: Buying from Mansam directly
What a customer asks: Why should I buy here rather than anywhere else?
The one-line answer (EN): Every boutique and this website are the house's own. What reaches you comes straight from Mansam — the same hands that made it — so what you wear is Mansam entirely.
Never say: NEVER mention counterfeits, fakes, copies or the grey market. Never say or imply that any other seller is not genuine, and never name one. State what is true of us; say nothing about anyone else.

ID: BEN-13
Status: ON
Category / item: Authenticity
What a customer asks: Is this genuine? How do I know it is real Mansam?
The one-line answer (EN): You have our word on it. It comes to you from the house directly, and every piece is exactly as it was composed and filled.
Never say: NEVER discuss counterfeits, how to spot them, or what others sell. If she presses about something bought elsewhere, that is for customer care — we cannot speak for what we did not sell.
